tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

pubo-scope-two-problems: Sec. I, p.2: 'We concentrate on two problems: (a) the MaxCut problem on weighted graphs, and (b) the LABS problem. In both cases we map the problem onto an Ising-type Hamiltonian.'
pubo-definition: Sec. I, p.2: the paper describes PUBO as the more general class that contains QUBO. A brief descriptive definition, but it is the paper's own use of the term.
method-linear-ansatz-product-start: Sec. II, Eq. (2)-(6), p.3: the paper states the linear Ansatz in Y_j, the product initial state of X and Z eigenstates, S = I so a = b, and that the updates commute. These are the paper's own method choices with the consequences stated in the text.
method-tau-selection: Sec. II, p.3: 'In the results shown in the following sections, the value of the small imaginary time parameter tau is chosen by increasing...' with the stopping rule stated. Protocol statement.
maxcut-ar-definition: Sec. III, p.3: 'we define the approximation ratio (AR) as the energy obtained by QITE divided by the lowest energy produced by GW', with the reason given.
maxcut-itd-edges: Sec. III, Eq. (11), p.3-4: states the ITD edge scheme as used, 'as in [17]': an initially vanishing subgraph weight grown until H_w[s] -> H_w.
maxcut-test-setup: Sec. III, p.4: weighted NWS graphs with k = 4, p = 0.5, weights uniform on (0,1], linear Ansatz with 1 ITD edge, AR and P(GS) as the measures. Stated test set-up.
maxcut-more-itd-edges-open: Sec. III, p.5: the authors say they chose 1 ITD edge, that more edges or another scheme might do better on larger graphs, and that 500+ vertex scaling is under study. They state this about their own work.
labs-definition: Sec. IV, Eq. (12), p.5: defines the LABS goal as minimizing the sidelobe energy of N spins with autocorrelation A_k.
labs-is-pubo: Sec. V, p.7 and Eq. (13), p.5: the LABS Hamiltonian is given with Z Z Z Z quartic terms and the authors call it a PUBO problem for that reason. Follows directly from the stated Hamiltonian.
labs-itd-coefficients: Sec. IV, Eq. (15)-(17), p.5-6: states the ITD coefficient alpha[s] on the quartic terms and the beta[s] range parameter as the paper's own method.
labs-test-setup: Sec. IV, p.6, Fig. 5-6: the text says 40 steps, 50 random |0>/|+> initial states, 6 <= N <= 21; Fig. 5 caption says 100 states and 6 <= N <= 28; Fig. 6 caption says 6 <= N <= 18. The value reports all three as the paper states them. The paper is internally inconsistent, so the coordinator should treat the exact ranges with care.
labs-tested-below-qaoa-advantage-range: Sec. IV, p.6-7: 'the scaling advantage of QAOA ... was found in the range of 28 <= N <= 40, which is larger than the problem sizes we tested. Therefore, we need to investigate...' A limit on their own coverage.
quadratic-ansatz-definition: Sec. IV, Eq. (18)-(20), p.6: defines A_quad with linear and quadratic Y terms, the vector of length N(N+1)/2, S a = b, and S = I for the product start.
quadratic-ansatz-cost-and-scope-limit: Sec. IV, p.7: 'The quadratic Ansatz simulation requires significantly more computational resources and precision than the linear Ansatz' and benefits may lie 'beyond our current resources to test'. Stated limits of their own work.
qite-classically-simulable: Sec. III p.5 and Sec. V p.7: 'QITE with a linear Ansatz can be simulated efficiently classically'. The authors admit this about their own method. It follows from the product initial state and commuting single-qubit updates of Sec. II.
step-to-solution-definition: Sec. III A, Eq. (9), p.5: S = log(0.01)/log(1 - P(GS)) is defined as the average number of register layout optimization steps for 99% certainty.
qaoa-seed-dependence-limitation: Sec. III B, p.6: 'on larger graphs these results depend stronger on the initial random seed. Because of this we have outliers where the optimization fails to converge for specific seeds.' The authors report this about their own runs.
qaoa-lattice-setup: Sec. III B, p.6: atoms at fixed lattice points instead of FR placement, random graphs with 10 to 13 vertices from square and honeycomb lattices, the IEEE 9-bus graph, two graphs per lattice. Stated set-up.
qaoa-numerical-simulation-setup: Sec. III B, p.6 and Fig. 5 caption: results are by simulating QuEra's hardware, 5 layers up to 1000 Adam steps, 10 layers up to 2000. The body text also mentions 15 layers, which the value does not claim.
local-detuning-eliminates-linear-z: Sec. III B, Eq. (10)-(11), p.5-6: 'by setting the local detuning parameters to Delta_i = 2 sum_j w_ij, we can completely eliminate the linear Z terms'. Follows directly from the Hamiltonian as written; the Discussion repeats it.
qaoa-mixer-amplitude-setup: Sec. III B, p.6, before Eq. (14): the mixer uses Omega(t) = 2 MHz. The remark 'best performing value for smaller graphs' is an unsupported aside, but the value reports it as the authors' statement.
edge-weights-from-line-impedance: Sec. II, Eq. (1), p.3: w_ij = 1/sqrt(R_ij^2 + X_ij^2) for connected nodes, 0 otherwise, with the data from IEEE test cases [23].
maxcut-cost-function-definition: Sec. III, Eq. (3)-(4), p.3: defines weighted MaxCut as a QUBO with cost C = sum w_ij Z_i Z_j, minimized by evolving a Rydberg array under H(t).
adiabatic-ansatz-and-hardware-bounds: Sec. III A, Eq. (5), p.3-4: adiabatic-type Ansatz, t_max = 4 us, amplitude 0 at both ends, bounds 0 <= Omega <= 2.51 MHz and |Delta| <= 19.89 MHz. Stated set-up.
layout-selection-procedure: Sec. III A, p.3-4: N_R random FR-based layouts, initial cost measured after adiabatic evolution with default parameters, lowest-cost layout kept for pulse optimization. The paper's own protocol.
pulse-optimizer-and-shots-setup: Sec. III A, p.4: optimization steps simulated with Pennylane's Jax interface and Nadam, then optimized pulses run on Aquila with 1000 shots.
fidelity-estimation-setup: Sec. IV, Fig. 6 and text, p.6-7: IEEE 9-bus graph from |0>^N, 16 cycles of 0.25 us, 1000 shots on Aquila, 100,000 on a noiseless simulator, three repeats for error bars.
scope-weighted-maxcut-only: Sec. II, p.2-3: 'In this work, we identified our optimization problem of interest as solving weighted MaxCut problems and left other optimization problems in power systems as future work.'
rydberg-sim-not-hardware: Sec. V, p.8: 'Since our optimization was performed on a simulator instead of the Aquila hardware, it is important to study the performance when the optimization is performed on actual hardware.' A limit the authors state about their own work.
qrnn-training-uses-postselection-not-amp: Sec. 3, p.9: the authors state they postselect instead of performing amplitude amplification and track the postselection probabilities. A protocol statement.
qrnn-classical-simulation-resources: Sec. 3, p.9-10: pytorch simulation and '2-8 CPUs, 500MB-35GB per core' stated as the authors' own run setup.
qrnn-qubit-count-formula: Fig. 5 caption, p.10: states the qubit count H + I + ord for the architecture as built, with H, I, ord defined in the caption and Sec. 2.2.
qrnn-neuron-order-and-activation: Sec. 2.2, p.6-7, eq. (2): the paper defines the neuron, its order ord >= 1 and its rotation f(theta). The construction is adopted from Cao et al. but defined here.
qrnn-higher-degree-neuron-generalization: Sec. 2.2, p.7-8, eq. (3), Fig. 3: the paper defines its own degree-d generalization and the AND example in the text.
qrnn-mnist-split: Sec. 4.3, p.12: the data split is stated as the paper's own protocol.
qrnn-feature-maps-train-only: Sec. 4.3, p.15: states that feature maps are fitted on the training set only and that PCA to 30 dimensions precedes t-SNE. Preprocessing protocol.
qrnn-dna-task-definition-and-metric: Sec. 4.5, p.16: the paper defines the task, stopping threshold 10^-3, batch of 128 and the step-count metric.
qrnn-dna-baseline-caveats: Sec. 4.5, p.17, footnotes 2 and 3: the authors state the RNN timeouts and restarts and that data above length 100 needs caution. Footnote 2 is an expectation but is a caveat on the comparison.
qrnn-no-state-of-the-art-claim: Sec. 1, p.4: the authors say the model does not yet compete with state-of-the-art scores on larger datasets. A limit on their own work.
qrnn-hardware-training-not-done: Sec. 3, p.9: the authors say they trained with pytorch autograd in simulation, and that hardware would need gradient-free or numerical gradients. The sentence is cut by a figure but both halves are legible. Stated limit of the simulation.
qrnn-mnist-reduced-input: Sec. 4.3, p.12: crop to 20x20, downscale to 10x10, binarize, length 100, and the authors' own remark that information is reduced and they do not compete with top classifiers.
qrnn-outclassed-by-classical-rnns: Sec. 5, p.17: the authors state that simple RNNs outclass the QRNN on real-world tasks and give the exponential classical memory cost as a part cause. A limit of their own work.
hweff-definition-hardware-efficient: Sec. I, p.2: 'In this work, we call hardware-efficient any variational quantum algorithm that (i)... or (ii)...'. An explicit own definition.
hweff-setup-trotter-pauli-hamiltonian: Sec. II, p.2: states the assumed Hamiltonian form (Pauli-string terms, real h_k, K ~ O(poly(n))) and the Trotter plus one-term-at-a-time variational protocol. The method set-up as the paper states it.
hweff-definition-objective-overlap: Sec. II, Eq. (1), p.2-3 and App. A: defines the per-term squared-distance error and the objective F_k. Equivalence derived in App. A.
hweff-derivation-cost-reduces-to-overlap: App. A, Eq. (A4)-(A5), p.9: the expansion is shown in full, with the constant-norm assumption stated (true for a PQC). Elementary algebra, complete in the paper.
hweff-derivation-real-time-objective-clo: App. A, Eq. (A6): uses H_l^2 = 1 and the series of e^A to get the cos/sin form; the step is shown. Elementary identity, complete in the paper.
hweff-derivation-imaginary-time-objectiv: App. A, Eq. (A7): same argument with cosh/sinh, 'following the same argument'. Elementary identity, complete in the paper.
hweff-setup-ansatz-depth-two: Sec. II p.4 and App. G, Fig. 10: the paper states D = 2 throughout, three CNOTs and Np = 15 per block, universal for two-qubit unitaries up to phase (the universality is credited to Ref. [65], but the value reports the construction used).
hweff-definition-pqc-parametrization: App. B, p.10: states the circuit form U = U_D...U_1 with fixed or exp(-i theta G) gates, G Hermitian with G^2 = 1. Definition of the object the proof covers.
hweff-theorem-sinusoidal-coordinatewise-: Sec. II p.4 and App. B (B1-B6), Fig. 9: the sinusoidal form A sin(x+B) is derived in the paper from U_d = cos(theta)1 - i sin(theta)G with the conditions stated. Prior work [36-39] had it for standard PQCs, but this variant is derived here.
hweff-derivation-update-rule-two-evaluat: App. B, Eq. (B4)-(B6), p.10-11: the arctan2 closed form from two evaluations pi/2 apart is derived in the paper, with the choice of k into (-pi, pi].
hweff-derivation-single-evaluation-recyc: App. C, Eq. (C1)-(C2), p.11: the identity f_{l,d}(theta_d) = A_{l,d-1} follows directly from the preceding update and is shown in the text.
hweff-definition-cone-update: Sec. II, p.4-5: 'We call this approach the cone update'; the O(Nb Np) controlled-gate count is stated with its terms defined.
hweff-definition-block-update: Sec. II, p.5: 'We call this approach the block update', with the tau/Nb time step stated.
hweff-definition-angle-update: Sec. II, p.5: 'We call this approach the angle update', with the tau/(NbNp) time step stated.
hweff-description-hadamard-test-cone: App. D, p.11-12: the circuit construction (ancilla, controlled local differences, Z x H expectation, phase gate for the imaginary part, O(NbNp) controlled operations) is described and the result shown in the text.
hweff-scope-angle-update-direct-measurem: Sec. II, p.5 and App. E: the authors state that angle update can drop the ancilla via direct measurements (credited to Refs. [52,53]) at the cost of additional circuits. A statement of what their method covers.
hweff-limit-angle-update-ancilla-version: App. E, p.12: the authors say the ancilla-based angle update still needs an ancilla and a controlled operation that may be hard on current hardware. A limit of their own algorithm.
hweff-derivation-angle-update-direct-exp: App. E, Eq. (E1)-(E7), p.12-13: the closed forms with two (real time) and three (imaginary time) expectations are derived in the paper ('a direct calculation shows').
hweff-derivation-tdvp-linear-system: App. F, Eq. (F6)-(F8), p.13-14: the linear system Re(A)B = Im(C) is derived by minimizing the squared distance over real parameter velocities. The remark that imaginary time gives similar systems is cited to [16], but it is a side remark.
hweff-setup-objective-accuracy-experimen: Sec. III A, p.6, Fig. 6: Ansatz D = 2, periodic boundary conditions, random parameters, time steps 0.1, 0.1/(NsNb), 0.1/(NsNbNp), 3 blocks/45 parameters and 5 blocks/75 parameters, 25 random states. All stated as the paper's own set-up.
hweff-setup-ising-imaginary-time-experim: Sec. III C, p.6-7, Fig. 7: n = 8, D = 2, open boundary conditions, tau = 0.1, 20 random initializations, lambda = 1 and 4. Stated as the paper's own set-up.
hweff-limit-simulation-noise-free: App. G, p.15: 'Expectations and Hadamard tests are calculated exactly. We do not include finite-sampling noise or hardware noise.' qutip named. A limit of the simulations.
hweff-setup-numerical-qubit-range: App. G, p.14: D = 2, n in {4, 6, 8}, causal cones of at most six qubits, also with periodic boundaries. Stated set-up.
hweff-setup-trotter-formulas-ising-split: App. G, Eq. (G1)-(G4), p.14-15: first- and second-order Trotter formulas and the ZZ / X split of the Ising chain are stated as the formulas used.
born-machine-definition: Sec. III, p.4: defines the Born machine q(z) = |<z|psi(theta)>|^2 on n-bit strings and the amortized form with x as extra parameters.
kl-objective-definition: Sec. IV A, Eq. (2), p.5: the KL objective is defined as the OPVI choice h = identity with the stated operator, under the stated assumption p(z|x) > 0. The zero minimum at the true posterior is the standard property of KL and is stated alongside.
adversarial-ratio-estimation-method: Sec. IV A, p.5-6, Eq. (4)-(7): the authors define their classifier-based ratio estimate for the implicit Born machine and the resulting objective L_KL.
stein-operator-definition: Sec. IV B, p.6: 'A Stein operator is independent from q and is characterized by having zero expectation under the true posterior for all functions f in the chosen family'. The paper's own definition.
stein-operator-valid-binary-proof: App. C, Eq. (C1)-(C4), p.12: 'Here we prove that...' for any f and any p(z|x) > 0 on {0,1}^n. The cancellation is shown term by term and concludes 'a valid Stein operator'.
sprinkler-setup-instances-ansatz: Sec. V A, p.7: 30 random sprinkler networks with entries from U[0.01, 0.99], conditioning on 'Grass wet' true, three-qubit hardware-efficient ansatz, S(x) = H x H x H, parameters near 0. All stated as the paper's own setup.
sprinkler-setup-training: Sec. V A, p.7-8, Fig. 6: MLP 3-6-1, 100 plus 100 samples, SGD batch ten, rate 0.03, Born machine 100 samples per expectation, rate 0.003, 1000 epochs, bootstrap 68% interval. Stated protocol.
tvd-not-efficiently-computable: Sec. V A, p.8: 'We emphasize that TVD cannot be efficiently computed in general and can be shown only for small examples.' The authors state a limit on their evaluation metric.
hmm-setup: Sec. V B, p.8-9, Eq. (15)-(16): T = 8, Bernoulli latent chain, Gaussian observations, one amortized eight-qubit Born machine with Rx(x_t) encoding, MLP 16-24-1, 3000 epochs, rates 0.006 and 0.03. Stated setup.
hmm-classically-tractable: Sec. V B, p.9: 'inference in this HMM can be performed exactly and efficiently with classical algorithms'. The authors admit the demonstrated task is classically tractable. The Viterbi and factorial-HMM costs are supporting field facts (Ref. [113]) and do not change that admission.
lung-cancer-setup: Sec. V C, p.9: five-qubit ibmq rome, conditioning on X, D and I, five latent variables on five qubits, L = 2 ansatz, 1024 shots, classifier with five inputs and ten ReLU units, KL objective. Stated setup.
lung-cancer-network-modified: Sec. V C and App. F, p.9 and 13: the network is 'slightly modified'; 'either' is replaced by 'illness' through additive smoothing because the derivation assumes nonzero posteriors. A stated change to the paper's own test case.
adversarial-method-requirements-and-risk: Sec. VI, p.10: the authors say adversarial training 'may be challenging due to the large number of hyperparameters and well-known stability issues' and state the three requirements. A caveat on their own method.
appendix-a-learnability-open: App. A, p.11-12: 'we are discussing only representational power and not learnability'. The open-question sentence is a field remark, but the scope statement is the paper's own.
born-machines-two-vi-methods: Abstract, p.1: states that they use Born machines as variational distributions and adopt the adversarial and kernelized Stein discrepancy realizations. Sec. IV A and IV B develop both.
ksd-method-needs-explicit-priors: Sec. VI, p.10: 'A limitation of this approach is that it requires explicit priors and likelihoods.' The authors state it about their own method.

theory_low.qrnn-linearity-of-unitary-circuits: Sec. 2.2, p.5: general background about quantum mechanics, stated without proof or citation. A field statement, not a result of this paper.
theory_low.qrnn-neuron-amplification-overhead-bound: App. A.1, p.24: the bound is called 'easy to derive' and is only sketched in one line. It is loose and not proved in the paper.
theory_low.hweff-table1-hardware-comparison: Table I, p.5: the authors' own big-O counts, listed without a derivation in the text. The tdvp column is their reading of the cited Ref. [16].
theory_low.hweff-derivation-tdvp-measurement-scalin: Sec. III, App. F, Eq. (F9)-(F10): a first-order perturbation bound that ignores delta A delta B and is stated for the worst case. It is an upper bound, not a proved scaling, and it takes the O(1/sqrt(m)) element error as given.
theory_low.hweff-conclusion-tdvp-cost-kappa-squared: App. F, p.14: a conclusion drawn from the worst-case first-order bound in (F10). It describes a cited method, and the authors say the cost 'can be challenging'.
theory_low.optimal-classifier-gradient-vanishes: App. B, Eq. (B1)-(B3), p.11-12: what the text shows is that one product-rule term, sum_z q d log q, is zero. The value says the gradient of the expectation vanishes, which reads as the whole gradient, but the nonzero first term still gives the gradient in (B5). The argument is short, assumes an optimal discriminator, and the sentence overstates it.
theory_low.parameter-shift-gradient-adversarial: App. B, Eq. (B4)-(B5), p.12: relies on the parameter shift rule, cited to Refs. [126-128] and not proved here, and on the vanishing-term argument in (B2)-(B3). B5 is assembled from these. Not a result proved in the paper.
theory_low.ksd-gradient-parameter-shift: App. D, p.12-13: the gradient 'was derived in Ref. [43]' and the last step uses the cited parameter shift rule (B4). The remarks on simple form and sampling are authors' interpretation. Not proved in this paper.
